READING ROOM ACCESS LOG — 2 AUGUST 2029

· Cause of death: lack of air (asphyxia).
· Petechial haemorrhages inside the eyelids and on the face; not explained by a picture of heart failure.
· Slight abrasions around the mouth and nose; cotton fabric fibre in the mouth, consistent with the pillowcase.
· Fresh, faint bruising on both wrists: he was held.
· Estimated time of death: 21.30 – 23.00.

DNA RESULT — PILLOWCASE
A man who died in prison was named as the informant; Stefan Hahn’s defence rested on that claim.
Günter Albrecht’s name went into the file as the informant. His daughter stopped speaking to him.
Lerche’s identity remained open; publication of the memoir was halted by the court.
The archive added a page to Werner Albrecht’s personal file: “The informant code name in this file belongs to the file holder himself.” Forty years on, Günter Albrecht went to his brother’s funeral.
Günter Albrecht was taken into custody. His brother’s memoir was published; Günter went down in history as Lerche.
Ingrid was questioned and her inheritance frozen. The final chapter of the memoir was never found.
The death was accepted as natural. A year later Werner Albrecht’s memoir was published with the note “final chapter missing”.
Stefan Hahn was arrested for murder. At the hearing all he asked was that his father’s file be read in full. It was.

For forty years Günter was taken for the informant; on 10 March he was in Rostock, and that evening he did not go to his brother’s door.
Ingrid left her father at 18.00, and she was the one who insisted the death was not natural.
The petechial haemorrhages, the fibre in the mouth and the bruising on the wrists point to smothering.
He learned at the archive that Werner had informed on his father, called that evening and came; his skin was on the pillowcase, and the final chapter of the memoir was on his desk.

Berlin State Records Archive. Requested by: Werner Albrecht. Delivered: 18 July 2029. Names of third parties redacted.

· 3 March 1981 · IM “Lerche” report: “Three people in Albrecht’s kitchen: Albrecht, his brother ████ and ████. A plan to flee to the West was discussed. Date: 21 March, place: a boat in Köpenick.”
· 10 March 1981 · IM “Lerche” report: “Two people in Albrecht’s kitchen: Albrecht and ████. His brother is out of town this week. ████ arranged the boat; the money is from Albrecht.”
· 20 March 1981 · detention: Albrecht and ████.
· Sentence: Albrecht 3 years; ████ 6 years.

Note (personal version): The informant’s code name is visible; the real name may be disclosed only to the relatives of the victim concerned, not to the file holder.
SUSPICIOUS DEATH
ARCHIVE FILE — WERNER ALBRECHT (PERSONAL VERSION, REDACTED)
BDS Berlin — Kreuzberg Branch
Lichtenberg — prefab block, 11th floor
Suspicious death
His daughter
With his brother.
I haven’t talked about this for forty years.
Forty years on. In those years I was a man working in a factory. I knew about Dieter and my brother’s plan, yes. But I didn’t inform.
His voice calm, his hand trembling.
Your brother accused you of being the informant.
The factory had sent me to the shipyard in Rostock, for a week. When I came back my brother had been arrested. I don’t remember the dates, but we had a work calendar; it’ll be in the factory archive.
Where were you in March 1981?
At home, in Marzahn, with my wife. I didn’t want to see my brother’s face again.
Where were you on the evening of 9 August?
Günter Albrecht — interview

At bube Berlin’s lawful request, a single page.

· 10 March 1981 · IM “Lerche” report — the informant’s real name: Werner Albrecht.
“Only Hahn and I were in the kitchen; my brother is in Rostock. Hahn arranged the boat. I have to come too, or it will draw suspicion. My request: that my sentence be short and his long.”

Additional note: Werner Albrecht was released in 1984; Dieter Hahn died in prison the same year.
ARCHIVE FILE — DIETER HAHN (NEXT-OF-KIN VERSION), 10 MARCH 1981
With his daughter.
My father would have known that.
He didn’t speak for a week. Then at a family dinner he accused my uncle in front of everyone: ‘You were Lerche. There were three of us in that kitchen.’ My uncle left the table.
What happened when your father read the file?

He’d been writing it for forty years. After the file he wrote every night; ‘when the book comes out everyone will know,’ he said. The pages of the last chapter are missing; only the first half was left on the desk.
She stroked the edge of the draft.
What is the memoir draft on the desk?
I left his dinner at six. ‘Someone’s coming this evening, an old score,’ he said. I thought he meant my uncle.
Did you see your father yesterday evening?
Ingrid Albrecht — interview
The block’s lift car camera. 9 August 20.30 – 23.30.

THE REDACTED LINE  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH

A 79-year-old man who had just received his file from the old regime is found dead in his flat in Lichtenberg. The doctor says “heart”; his daughter says “my uncle informed on him”. The names in the file are redacted.

Petra Neumann — interview

Every file has several versions. In the personal version, third parties are redacted. A victim’s relative, reading their own relative’s file, can see the informant’s real name. The same report sits on two different desks with two different faces.
Is there another version of this file?
Last month the son of another victim of the same 1981 incident came to the reading room. After reading, he sat outside on the steps for half an hour. You’ll find his name in the access log.
Has anyone else come recently about the events in this file?

On 10 August 2029 at 08.15 in Lichtenberg, Werner Albrecht (79) was found dead in bed in his flat on the 11th floor of a prefab block. Found by: his daughter, Ingrid Albrecht.

Duty doctor’s first note: “Age-related heart failure.” On his daughter’s objection the file was passed to bube Berlin: the door was not locked, and on the living room table were a scattered archive file and an unfinished memoir draft.

Daughter’s statement: “Three weeks ago my father received his own file from the old regime. Since that day he’d been fighting with my uncle Günter. My uncle informed on him.”
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the reading room access log
Request Günter Albrecht’s 1981 work calendar
Request a DNA comparison of the pillowcase
Request the next-of-kin version of Dieter Hahn’s file
Examine the memoir draft on the desk
Request the search record for Stefan Hahn’s flat
Request Werner Albrecht’s phone record

Pankow, 11 August 2029.

· On the desk, a 128-page typed and handwritten stack; page numbers 213–340. Title: “Final chapter: Lerche”. Notes in the margins in Werner Albrecht’s hand.
· In the stack, a draft of a forged document “proving” that his brother Günter, not Werner Albrecht, was the informant.
· The 10 March 1981 page Stefan Hahn obtained from the archive, in the same folder.
SEARCH RECORD — STEFAN HAHN’S FLAT
On the access log.
I won’t talk without my lawyer.
I waited forty-five years. I saw the name of the man who informed on my father. It was Werner Albrecht himself, the ‘victim’ everyone knew. And now he was writing a book blaming his brother.
His jaw tightened.
On 2 August you read your father’s file.
Stefan Hahn — interview
I called. I wanted to talk. He hung up. I didn’t go.
Did you see Werner Albrecht on the evening of 9 August?
On the camera, the phone and the DNA.
He’d lain down on the bed and said, ‘Go.’ The pillow… I don’t know how long. Then I took the last chapter. That lie was not going to be printed.
He closed his eyes.
And then?

I went. I showed him the page. He laughed. ‘No one will believe it,’ he said, ‘my book is coming out, my document is ready, Günter will go down in history as Lerche.’ My father went down in history as nothing.
His voice broke.
Your skin is on the pillowcase.
Stefan Hahn — second interview

The 10 March report in the redacted file said “his brother is out of town”; Günter’s work calendar put him in Rostock that week — of the two people in the kitchen, one was the informant and the other was Hahn, who was arrested. The archivist and the access log led to Stefan Hahn, and the next-of-kin version to Lerche’s name. The phone, the lift camera, the DNA on the pillowcase and the search record closed the night.
A redacted line still carries information: who was absent, how many were there. Look not at whom a record accuses, but at who could have been there.
Lichtenberg and the Berlin State Records Archive — 1981 / 2029

In 1981, under the code name “Lerche”, Werner Albrecht informed on the escape he had planned with Dieter Hahn, and asked for his own sentence to be short. Hahn died in prison; Werner lived. Forty-eight years later he received his own file in redacted form and set about writing a memoir naming his brother Günter as the informant. Dieter Hahn’s son, Stefan, saw the informant’s real name in his father’s file. On the evening of 9 August he went to Werner, was met with Werner’s mockery, and smothered him with a pillow; he took the memoir’s final chapter with him.
Who is responsible for Werner Albrecht’s death?
